newsitem.title: USA: Air France, JAL start Atlanta cargo services.
newsitem.headline: Air France, JAL start Atlanta cargo services.

text.p: Air France and Japan Air Lines will begin freighter services out of Atlanta's Hartsfield International Airport in a few weeks, a Hartsfield official told Reuters Monday.
"We're adding five widebody freighters per week," Robert Kennedy, cargo development officer at Hartsfield said.
Japan Air Lines will begin freighter service April 1 and Air France April 6, Kennedy said. Both will use Boeing 747 aircraft.
Air France will fly between Paris and Atlanta and JAL to Hong Kong, Singapore and other Asian points.
Kennedy said another Asian and a Latin American airline are expected to begin to use Hartsfield "by late summer," but he declined to identify them.
In 1996, 572,264 tons of cargo came through Hartsfield, up five percent from the year ago, with international cargo up 11 percent, he said.
Hartsfield handles 280 freighter flights per day, including those of integrators such as Federal Express Corp and United Parcel Service.
The airport projects that in 1999 cargo will reach 735,988 tons.
To accommodate this growth, Hartsfiled is adding a new four building cargo complex that will total 400,000 square feet when completed by year-end, Kennedy said.
"We need more room, especially for widebody aircraft," he said.

Lufthansa Airlines, which flies a daily passenger and three weekly freighter flights to Hartsfield, is said to want to build its own cargo facility, but Kennedy would say only that an unidentified airline was discussing such plans.
Hartsfield also has plans for another 130,000 square foot building, but is studying the best location for it.
MartinAir began McDonnell Douglas MD-11 freighter service once weekly from Ecuador and once weekly from Costa Rica through Hartsfield in January.
"Those flights have been great," said Kennedy.
"We moved 7,000 tons of flowers in the first seven weeks of that flight," he said.
Kennedy said Hartsfield is a good gateway for Latin America due to its proximity to both Latin America and its short trucking distances to most of the United States.
Although Miami International Airport, Latin America's main air hub, is closer to Latin America, trucking distances are farther.
"We can truck to Chicago overnight," Kennedy said.
Hartsfiled is also an ideal transshipment point for Europe and Asia, Kennedy said. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax+5017
